text: George Washington. Wooden teeth.
Nope. No wood at all.
Washington: the wooden teeth myth.
His teeth were terrible.
By 1789, he had one tooth left.
So he wore dentures.
Made of hippo ivory.
Cow teeth. Horse teeth.
Metal springs and lead.
And human teeth.
Some were bought from enslaved people at Mount Vernon.
The springs pushed his jaws apart.
He had to clamp his mouth shut.
That's the tight-lipped face on the one dollar bill.
So where did the wood come from?
Ivory stains and cracks over time.
Old dentures can look like wood grain.
Also, wood would rot in your mouth.
Teeth made of wood: zero.
Anyway, here's Washington with his wooden teeth.
